Let's craft answer.

## TL;DR  
Yes – you can validate a Mapbox‑style JSON against the **MapLibre‑compatible style spec** with a single command‑line call. The most common way is to use the **`@mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec`** (or its fork `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec`) npm package:

```bash
# 1️⃣ Install the validator globally (once)
npm install -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec   # or @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec

# 2️⃣ Run it on your style file
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate path/to/style.json
# (or: maplibre-gl-style-spec validate path/to/style.json)
```

The command prints **errors**, **warnings**, and a short **summary**. If the exit code is `0` the file is fully spec‑compliant; any non‑zero exit code means you have something that MapLibre will reject (or at least warn about).

Below is a step‑by‑step guide, plus a few extra sanity‑checks that are specific to the Mapbox‑to‑MapLibre migration.

---

## 1️⃣ Install the validator

You only need Node ≥ 12 (the validator works on any recent Node version).  
Pick one of the two packages:

| Package | Why you might choose it |
|---------|------------------------|
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec` | The original, battle‑tested validator. Works for any style that follows the **Mapbox GL JS v1** spec (the same spec MapLibre uses). |
| `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` | A thin fork that bumps the version number to match the MapLibre release cadence. Functionally identical for validation. |

```bash
# Global install (makes the CLI available anywhere)
npm install -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec
# or
npm install -g @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec
```

> **Tip:** If you prefer not to install globally, you can add the package to a project (`npm i -D @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec`) and run it via `npx`:

```bash
npx mapbox-gl-style-spec validate style.json
```

---

## 2️⃣ Run the validator

```bash
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate ./my-exported-style.json
```

Typical output looks like:

```
✔ style.json is a valid Mapbox GL style (0 errors, 2 warnings)

Warnings:
  - source "my-source" uses a Mapbox proprietary URL (mapbox://)
  - glyphs URL points to a Mapbox endpoint (https://api.mapbox.com/fonts/v1/...)
```

*Exit code:*  
- `0` → no errors (warnings are fine, you can still deploy).  
- `1` → at least one **error** (the style will not load in MapLibre).  

You can also ask for a **JSON report** (handy for CI pipelines):

```bash
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate style.json --output json > validation-report.json
```

---

## 3️⃣ What the validator actually checks

The validator enforces the **style specification** (layers, sources, paint/layout properties, expressions, etc.). It does **not** know anything about your runtime environment (e.g., whether a custom source URL is reachable). The checks include:

| Category | Example checks |
|----------|----------------|
| **Top‑level fields** | `version` must be `8`; `center`, `zoom`, `bearing`, `pitch` must be numbers; `glyphs` must be a string URL. |
| **Sources** | Required keys (`type`, `url`/`tiles`); correct property types per source type (`vector`, `raster`, `geojson`, `image`, `video`). |
| **Layers** | Valid `id`, `type`, `source`, `source-layer`; correct paint/layout property names for the layer type; expression syntax validation. |
| **Expressions** | Proper number of arguments, correct data types, no unknown functions. |
| **Deprecated / removed properties** | Flags usage of properties that were removed after v1.13 (e.g., `text-font` on symbol layers). |
| **Schema version** | Guarantees the style conforms to the **Mapbox GL JS v1** schema, which is exactly what MapLibre‑GL v1.x expects. |

If the validator reports **errors**, they are usually things that will cause MapLibre to refuse to render the style (e.g., a typo in a paint property, a missing required source field, an expression that uses a Mapbox‑only function).

---

## 4️⃣ Migration‑specific checks (beyond the spec)

Even when the style passes the spec validator, a Mapbox‑style often contains **Mapbox‑only resources** that MapLibre cannot fetch. The validator will flag them as *warnings* (or you can add a quick post‑process script). Common culprits:

| Resource | What to look for | How to fix |
|----------|------------------|------------|
| **Mapbox source URLs** | `source.type === "vector"` && `source.url.startsWith("mapbox://")` | Replace with a self‑hosted vector tile endpoint (e.g., `https://mytileserver.com/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`). |
| **Glyphs** | `glyphs` points to `https://api.mapbox.com/fonts/v1/...` | Use an open‑source font service (e.g., `https://fonts.openmaptiles.org/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf`) or host your own. |
| **Sprite** | `sprite` points to a Mapbox CDN URL | Host the sprite sheet yourself (`https://mycdn.com/sprite`). |
| **Terrain source** | `source.type === "raster-dem"` && `source.url` is a Mapbox terrain URL | Switch to an open DEM source (e.g., `https://tiles.opentopomap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`). |
| **Mapbox proprietary expressions** | Functions like `["heatmap-weight", ...]` that rely on Mapbox data | Usually fine – they are part of the spec – but double‑check any custom functions you added. |

### Quick “Mapbox‑URL” scanner

If you want an automated check that runs after the spec validator, add a tiny Node script (or a one‑liner) to your CI:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
STYLE=$1
if grep -qE 'mapbox://|api.mapbox.com' "$STYLE"; then
  echo "❌ Found Mapbox‑only URLs in $STYLE"
  exit 1
else
  echo "✅ No Mapbox URLs detected"
fi
```

Run it together with the spec validator:

```bash
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate style.json && ./check-mapbox-urls.sh style.json
```

---

## 5️⃣ Using the validator in CI/CD pipelines

Because the CLI returns a proper exit code, you can drop it straight into GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, etc.

**GitHub Actions example**

```yaml
name: Validate MapLibre style

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  style-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install validator
        run: npm install -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec
      - name: Validate style.json
        run: |
          mapbox-gl-style-spec validate ./styles/style.json
```

If the style is invalid, the job fails and the PR cannot be merged until you fix the errors.

---

## 6️⃣ Alternative tools (if you prefer a GUI)

| Tool | CLI? | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| **Maputnik** | No (web UI) | Loads a style, shows validation errors in the sidebar. Great for interactive debugging. |
| **mapbox-gl-js** (runtime) | Yes (via Node) | `new mapboxgl.Style(styleJson)` throws if the style is invalid. Less detailed than the spec validator. |
| **maplibre-gl-native** (C++) | No direct CLI, but ships a `style-validator` binary in some builds. Usually overkill for simple JSON checks. |

For most automated workflows, the npm‑based validator is the simplest and most reliable.

---

## 7️⃣ Summary checklist before you “deploy”

1. **Run the spec validator** – `mapbox-gl-style-spec validate style.json`.  
2. **Fix any errors** (the style will not load otherwise).  
3. **Address warnings** that reference Mapbox‑only URLs (glyphs, sprites, sources).  
4. (Optional) Run a **custom URL scanner** to guarantee no `mapbox://` or `api.mapbox.com` strings remain.  
5. **Test the style** in a local MapLibre‑GL instance (e.g., a tiny HTML page or Maputnik) to confirm visual fidelity.  
6. **Add the validator to CI** so future style edits are automatically checked.

---

## 8️⃣ One‑liner you can copy‑paste

```bash
npm install -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec && \
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate ./my-style.json && \
grep -qE 'mapbox://|api.mapbox.com' ./my-style.json && \
  { echo "❌ Mapbox URLs still present!"; exit 1; } || \
  echo "✅ Style is spec‑valid and free of Mapbox‑only URLs."
```

If the command finishes with `✅`, you’re good to push the style to your MapLibre deployment.

---

### Gotchas & FAQs

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Do I need to install MapLibre‑GL to validate?** | No. The validator works purely on the JSON and the spec definition. |
| **What version of the spec does it use?** | The validator follows the **Mapbox GL JS v1** spec (currently version 8). MapLibre‑GL v2+ is still based on the same spec, so it’s compatible. |
| **Can it validate raster‑DEM terrain sources?** | Yes – as long as the source definition conforms to the spec. It won’t check whether the URL actually serves DEM tiles. |
| **My style uses custom expressions (e.g., `["case", …]`). Will they be caught?** | The validator parses all expressions and will flag syntax errors, unknown functions, or type mismatches. |
| **I’m using a Docker image for CI – can I run the validator there?** | Absolutely. Just use a Node base image (`node:20-alpine`) and `npm i -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec`. |

---

### TL;DR Command (copy‑paste)

```bash
npm i -g @mapbox/mapbox-gl-style-spec   # install once
mapbox-gl-style-spec validate path/to/style.json   # run validation
```

If you prefer the MapLibre‑branded fork:

```bash
npm i -g @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec
maplibre-gl-style-spec validate path/to/style.json
```

That’s all you need to be confident that your exported style JSON will work with MapLibre before you push it to production. Happy mapping! 🚀
